items.stem: Complete the statement: An ideal standard is one that …
options: is based on last year's actual costs
assumes perfect operating conditions with no waste or idle time
can be achieved with normal effort and allows for normal losses
items.answer: assumes perfect operating conditions with no waste or idle time
items.markingKey: Ideal: no allowance for inefficiency; attainable: allows normal losses [1].

items.stem: Explain why attainable standards are usually preferred to ideal standards.
items.answer: Ideal standards are almost never met, so they produce constant adverse variances and demotivate staff; attainable standards are challenging but achievable, motivating workers and giving meaningful variances.
items.markingKey: Ideal demotivating [1]; attainable realistic/motivating [1]; useful variances [1] [3]

items.stem: Explain two difficulties in setting standard costs.
items.answer: Forecasting future prices (inflation, exchange rates); deciding on allowances for waste and idle time; rapid changes in technology or product design; obtaining reliable time studies.
items.markingKey: Two difficulties [1 each] + explanation [1 each] [4]

items.answer: Materials $7.50; labour $30.00; variable overhead $18.00; total $55.50

items.stem: Explain two uses of a standard costing system.
items.answer: Basis for budgets and pricing; control through variance analysis; valuing inventory; motivating staff with targets.

items.stem: Explain how employing more skilled workers could cause an adverse labour rate variance but a favourable labour efficiency variance.
items.answer: Skilled workers are paid more than the standard rate (adverse rate) but work faster and waste less time (favourable efficiency).

items.stem: Explain why variances should be investigated rather than simply recorded.
items.answer: Investigation finds the cause so that managers can correct problems (or update standards); only significant variances should be investigated where benefit exceeds cost.
items.markingKey: Find causes/corrective action [1]; significance/cost-benefit [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why a favourable fixed overhead volume variance does not mean that fixed costs were saved.
